notes.meaning: God remembered Noah and all the animals with him inside the ark. This does not mean God had forgotten them, but that He began to act kindly to keep His promise to them. God sent a wind across the earth, and the floodwaters began to go down.

The deep underground water springs and the floodgates of heaven were closed. The heavy rain from the sky completely stopped falling. God showed His control over nature by shutting down the forces that brought the flood.
The waters steadily drained away from the surface of the earth. After one hundred and fifty days, the water level dropped noticeably. God returned the waters step by step to their proper places.

The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. God safely guided the floating ship to land without any human steering. This gave Noah real peace of mind after months of drifting on the water.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Modern scholars note that Ararat refers to the ancient kingdom of Urartu near Lake Van, describing an entire mountainous region rather than one specific mountain peak.

notes.meaning: The waters kept going down until the tenth month arrived. On the first day of that month, the tops of the mountains could finally be seen. These rising peaks appeared like small islands, showing that God was steadily restoring the dry earth.

Noah waited patiently for forty days after the mountain peaks appeared. Then he opened the small window he had built into the ark. He was eager to see whether the earth was ready for his family again.

Noah sent out a raven to see how far the water had dropped. The raven flew back and forth, resting on the roof of the ark and feeding on floating carcasses. Because it did not mind living in the wet ruins, it gave Noah little clear news about the ground.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Christian teachers often saw the raven leaving the ark as a symbol of sin being cast out, or of self-seeking people who wander outside the care of the church.

notes.meaning: Noah then sent out a dove to see if the water had cleared from the lower ground. Doves fly lower than ravens and look for plants and seeds to eat. Noah knew the dove would quickly return if the valley soil was still buried under water.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Christian writers saw the dove as an image of the Holy Spirit and the ark as the Church, which welcomes the soul fleeing a sinful world.

notes.meaning: The dove found no dry, clean place to rest its feet, so it flew right back to the ark. Noah reached out his hand and pulled the tired bird back inside. Just as Noah welcomed the bird, God warmly welcomes those who seek safety in Him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Christian tradition often saw the dove returning to the ark as a symbol of faithful believers finding safety and rest inside the church.

notes.meaning: Noah waited seven more days before sending the dove out a second time. He showed great patience instead of rushing ahead of God. Waiting by seven-day periods suggests that Noah likely observed a regular weekly day of rest and worship aboard the ark.

The dove flew back to Noah in the evening, carrying a freshly plucked olive leaf in its beak. Olive trees grow down in the valleys, so this proved that the waters had drained away from the lower ground. The green olive leaf gave Noah fresh hope that peaceful life was returning to the world.

Noah waited another seven days and sent the dove out a third time. This time the dove did not return, because it found a dry home and plenty of food on the earth. Noah now had clear proof that the ground was ready for life.

On the first day of the new year, when Noah was six hundred and one years old, the water had dried from the ground. Noah removed part of the roof covering of the ark and saw dry land all around him. Even though the ground looked dry, he continued to wait for God's call before stepping outside.

By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the ground was thoroughly dry and firm. Noah had lived inside the ark for a full year and ten days. God made sure the earth was completely ready before letting Noah and his family live on it.

God spoke directly to Noah after many months of silence. Hearing God's voice brought comfort and direction to Noah after his long wait. God made sure Noah had clear instructions before taking his next step.

God told Noah to come out of the ark along with his wife, his sons, and their wives. Noah had waited for God's command to enter the ark, and he waited for God's command to leave it. We can trust God to show us the right time to move forward.

God ordered Noah to bring out every animal, bird, and crawling creature so they could fill the earth again. God gave them the blessing to spread out and have offspring, renewing His original plan for creation. This showed Noah that the terrible destruction of the flood was finally over.
Noah obeyed God and walked out of the ark with his entire family. All eight people stepped safely onto dry land with thankful hearts. Their rescue showed God's faithfulness to those who follow Him.

All the animals, birds, and creeping creatures left the ark in an orderly way, family by family. Not a single kind of creature that entered the ark was lost during the flood. God preserved every species so life could thrive across the earth once more.

The very first thing Noah did upon leaving the ark was build an altar and worship the Lord. He sacrificed some of the clean animals and birds as burnt offerings to thank God for saving his family. Noah chose to honor God with his few livestock before even building a home for himself.

God was pleased with Noah's heart and accepted his offering of thanksgiving. The Lord promised within Himself never again to curse the ground or wipe out all living creatures with a flood, even though human hearts are inclined toward sin from their youth. God chose to treat mankind with enduring mercy rather than immediate destruction.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching often translates this passage to describe humanity as prone to evil rather than having a completely corrupted nature.

notes.meaning: God promised that the rhythm of planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night will never fail as long as the earth exists. The flood had disrupted nature, but God firmly restored the seasons to care for all living things. We can count on God's constant faithfulness each day of the year.
